title: On the Computational Complexity of Hidden Markov Model Identification
abstract: arXiv:2610.09104v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Identification is the task of recovering the parameters of an unknown ground-truth model from sampled data. When parameters other than the ground truth induce the same output distribution, data alone does not provide enough information to recover the ground truth, and the model is thus called unidentifiable. We study the identifiability problem for hidden Markov models (HMMs): given an HMM, is it identifiable? Existing work on HMM identification establishes conditions under which the ground-truth HMM can be identified. However, most of these conditions are sufficient but not necessary, meaning that, when a model does not satisfy them, its identifiability remains inconclusive. We instead take a computational perspective: is there a sound and complete algorithm that decides whether a given HMM is identifiable, and if so, what is the complexity of this decision problem? translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.09104v1 公告类型：cross。摘要：辨识是指从未知采样数据中恢复真实模型参数的任务。当真实参数之外的其他参数也能诱导出相同的输出分布时，仅凭数据无法提供足够的信息来恢复真实参数，因此该模型被称为不可辨识的。我们研究隐马尔可夫模型（HMM）的可辨识性问题：给定一个HMM，它是否可辨识？现有的HMM辨识工作建立了真实HMM可以被辨识的条件。然而，这些条件大多是充分但不必要的，这意味着，当一个模型不满足这些条件时，其可辨识性仍然无法确定。我们转而从计算的角度来看待这一问题：是否存在一个可靠且完备的算法来判定给定的HMM是否可辨识？如果存在，该判定问题的复杂度是多少？我们考虑由各种……
tldr: 本文从计算复杂度的角度研究隐马尔可夫模型的可辨识性问题，旨在回答是否存在可靠且完备的算法来判定给定HMM是否可辨识，以及该判定问题的计算复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper takes a computational complexity perspective on the identifiability of hidden Markov models, investigating whether a sound and complete algorithm exists to decide whether a given HMM is identifiable, and what the complexity of this decision problem is.
